Description: TRUST-BC Unified pipeline, code release v1.1 (MIT licence; https://github.com/RezaAbolghasemi/TRUST-BC-Multicohort-Benchmark); developed by the authors in 2026. A separate model is fitted for each cohort: standardisation and PCA or random-forest feature selection (chosen per fold by inner cross-validation), followed by a soft-voting ensemble of class-balanced logistic regression and a Platt-calibrated linear support vector classifier. Survival branch (SEER): penalised Weibull accelerated failure time model (L2 penalty, λ = 0.1).

A predicted probability; a class label at the pre-specified threshold of 0.5; and a 95% split-conformal prediction set (singleton or ambiguous). Survival branch: predicted survival time and a high-/low-risk group defined by the training median.

A methodological benchmark and auditing template for evaluating breast cancer prediction models for preprocessing leakage, fixed-horizon label error, calibration and predictive uncertainty. Clinical use as auxiliary decision support is conceivable only after external validation and recalibration.
Researchers, model developers and clinical informatics teams; clinicians only within research settings.

Autonomous diagnosis, triage or treatment decisions. Screening populations (the Coimbra model was developed on a case–control sample). Use of SEER probabilities as absolute risks (they are overestimated about twofold). Patients outside the development populations, including women aged under 30 or over 69 years, node-negative disease, or settings that differ substantially from the 2006–2010 SEER cohort.

Data archetype (cytopathological, metabolic, registry). In SEER: race (White, Black, Other) and age group (under 50, 50–59, 60–69 years). Not evaluated: socioeconomic status, treatment, HER2 status, comorbidity, registry or geographic area, and screening setting.

Primary: accuracy (WBCD, Coimbra) and AUROC (SEER). Secondary: Brier score, expected calibration error, calibration slope, intercept and calibration-in-the-large, sensitivity, specificity, net benefit (decision curve analysis), conformal coverage and set sizes, and Harrell’s C-index (survival). Cross-validated CIs use the Nadeau–Bengio corrected variance; lockbox CIs use a stratified bootstrap or Wilson intervals.
Development sets (85%): WBCD 483 (180 events), Coimbra 98 (54 events), SEER 2,779 (389 deaths within 60 months). Survival training set: 3,219 (493 deaths). Dataset details in Section S12.

Repeated nested cross-validation on the development sets; a single evaluation on the held-out lockboxes: WBCD 86 (32 events), Coimbra 18 (10 events), SEER 491 (69 events); survival test set 805 (123 deaths).

Accuracy 97.08% (95% CI 95.34–98.82) for WBCD and 71.35% (62.27–80.43) for Coimbra; SEER AUROC 0.739 (0.709–0.769), expected calibration error 0.146, calibration-in-the-large −0.99 (pooled out-of-fold; Table 5). Conformal coverage 96.53%, 95.70% and 95.26%; ambiguous sets 0.90%, 72.10% and 38.08% (Table 2 and Section 3.3).

WBCD accuracy 100.00% (95.72–100.00); Coimbra accuracy 61.11% (38.62–79.69) and AUROC 0.725 (0.450–0.975); SEER AUROC 0.722 (0.646–0.790), sensitivity 36.23%, specificity 91.23%, Brier score 0.132. Survival C-index 0.722 (0.675–0.771) (Table 4 and Section 3.7).

SEER AUROC 0.738 (White), 0.729 (Black) and 0.765 (Other); 0.774 (under 50) to 0.699 (60–69 years). Calibration-in-the-large ranged from −0.40 (Black) to −1.44 (Other). Conformal coverage was 94.0–96.5% across subgroups but 69.9% among patients who died versus 99.4% among survivors (Table 5; Table S6).

Only public, de-identified data were used. Race is included as an established prognostic factor that reflects social and structural determinants rather than biology; because calibration differed by race, an uncorrected model could misstate risk unequally across groups.

Recalibrate before reporting absolute risks; consider class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction to equalise coverage for deaths; flag missing or out-of-range inputs for manual review; route ambiguous prediction sets to clinician review; perform external validation before any clinical use.

If deployed after validation: monitor input distributions against training ranges; track calibration (calibration-in-the-large and slope), discrimination and conformal coverage overall, by subgroup and by outcome class; use a rising ambiguous-set rate as an early warning of drift; re-evaluate after changes in staging editions, treatment practice or case mix; record model versions through repository releases.
